sections.name: Vengefly
sections.card:
Summary: A flying enemy that turns up in many areas, from King's Pass and the Forgotten Crossroads to Greenpath and the City of Tears. It drifts around a small stretch of air, squawks when you come into range, then flies straight at you. It is an easy enemy that shows up early.
Weak points: You can stand still and swing as it reaches you, or leap and attack downward onto it.
Tips: It never stops coming for you, so you can stay put and keep attacking until it falls. Only a few enemies reappear when you leave a room and come back, and this is one of them.

sections.name: Aspid Hunter
sections.card:
Summary: A floating enemy that wanders aimlessly until you approach, then spits blobs at you from a distance. It usually comes in groups. You meet it in the Forgotten Crossroads and in the western part of the Ancient Basin's tram tunnel.
Weak points: A short opening follows each spit, and the best response is to rush in close and hit it straight away.
Tips: Its wings make a whirring noise that carries a long way, so you can tell one is near before it comes into view. A stronger version, the Primal Aspid, is found in Kingdom's Edge. Leave the room and return, and it will be back, which few enemies do.

sections.name: Husk Guard
sections.card:
Summary: A husk with a club that stays where it stands until disturbed, then charges you. The Forgotten Crossroads holds only two: one just east of the False Knight's arena and one right above the north entrance to Crystal Peak.
Weak points: Strike right after its club slam, which is when it can be hurt. When it sends out its shockwave, jump over the wave, move in and you can usually land one or two hits. You can also tap it once and step out of reach before the club swings down, though the timing is tight and the Mothwing Cloak helps once you have it.
Tips: The club slam does two masks of damage. The backward hop throws a shockwave out to both sides along the ground, growing wider and faster as it travels. The guard you meet before the False Knight can be hit safely from the platform on the right. Each one drops 45 Geo, a lot this early, and both stand near the Stag Station, so they make an easy early source of Geo. Fight the one by the False Knight's arena soon, because it cannot be fought later in the game.

sections.name: Heavy Sentry
sections.card:
Summary: A walking corpse armed with a greatnail. It guards the City of Tears, where a small number are found, and two more stand in the eastern Royal Waterways.
Weak points: The best opening is during its charge: jump over it and strike downward, or cast Vengeful Spirit or Shade Soul, which it cannot avoid. A hit just after its plain overhead swing works too.
Tips: Its three attacks are an overhead swing, a charge with its nail held out in front, and a hop. If you try to jump over it, it hops up in reply, hurting on contact and then swinging down as it lands.

sections.name: Mantis Youth
sections.card:
Summary: A young mantis, one of the Mantis Tribe's children, that waits on a wall or the ceiling to ambush you. It is found only in Mantis Village and at its entrance.
Tips: When it notices you, it floats just outside nail range, winds up and lunges at you. The lunge covers little distance and is simple to avoid, but it drifts out of reach again straight away to wind up another one. Leave the room and return, and it will be back, which few enemies do.

sections.name: Soul Twister
sections.card:
Summary: A scholar from the Soul Sanctum that teleports about and shoots homing orbs at you. It is found east of the Soul Master's arena, and in the Trial of the Fool, during waves 9, 10, 11 and 17.
Weak points: It cannot teleport right after it fires, so let it shoot, dodge the orb by jumping over it or dashing, then run in and hit it. Great Slash, one of the Nail Arts, kills it quickly, and Dash Slash helps you cover the distance. Vengeful Spirit and Shade Soul also work from range, since it does not deliberately teleport away from them.
Tips: It teleports a lot and cannot be cornered. Luring it into small rooms or narrow halls leaves it fewer angles to attack from, so its orbs are easier to predict and you land more hits. Running away is very hard because it keeps teleporting after you, but it will not follow you through a screen transition into another room.

sections.name: Crystal Hunter
sections.card:
Summary: A floating enemy found nowhere but Crystal Peak. It usually keeps out of melee range and shoots crystals at you.
Weak points: Its shots come out after a short delay, so they usually miss you unless you are right underneath it. Leap up and slash at it while it is getting its next shot ready.
Tips: When its shot lands on a surface it bursts into a clump of crystals. The clump disappears after a short time, breaks easily with a nail hit, and can be bounced off with a nail strike. You can also knock the shot itself away with the nail, though it still passes through enemies.

sections.name: Great Hopper
sections.card:
Summary: The full-grown Hopper: a large enemy that hops nonstop, hurting you on contact and shaking the ground whenever it lands. You find it in the southeast of Kingdom's Edge and during the Trial of the Conqueror, and the dummy in Oro's backyard sets two on you when struck.
Weak points: Stay put and shuffle slightly sideways so each jump misses you, and each time it lands you can strike it safely. Howling Wraiths or Abyss Shriek can hit it while it is still in the air.
Tips: Touching it hurts. It swings round to go after you, which a regular Hopper does not do.

sections.name: Baldur
sections.card:
Summary: A young, crawling creature that defends itself by curling into a ball, which it rolls toward you. It lives in the Howling Cliffs, the Ancestral Mound and the Crystallised Mound; a stronger kind, the Sharp Baldur, shows up at the Colosseum of Fools.
Weak points: Jump over it as it closes in and strike down while you are above it. The Heavy Blow charm or the Quick Slash charm can instead keep knocking it back so it never touches you.
Tips: In its ball form it rebounds off the walls and off other Baldurs, then after a little while it opens up and turns toward you again.
Looks like: Its eyes are orange in the game.

sections.name: Gruz Mother
sections.card:
Summary: A boss that sleeps in a small arena in the Forgotten Crossroads, blocking the direct way down to an abandoned village. A hit wakes her, and the Trial of the Warrior finishes with two more of her at once.
Weak points: Her health is low, and Vengeful Spirit is the easiest tool against her: six casts, or 18 strikes with the Old Nail, will finish her.
Tips: Her Wild Slam, in which she throws herself again and again between floor and ceiling, is fast and needs decent timing to avoid, which the Mothwing Cloak helps with. When she dies in the Crossroads she releases a swarm of 7 or 8 Gruzzers, and you must kill them all before you can leave the arena. In the Trial of the Warrior two come at once: kill one as fast as you can, and Abyss Shriek or Howling Wraiths works best.

sections.name: Lumafly Lantern
sections.card:
Summary: An item that helps you see in dark areas. Sly sells it in Dirtmouth for 1800 Geo.
Uses: In dark areas it also lets you pay tolls that open benches and doors.
Tips: The toll gate between the Forgotten Crossroads and Crystal Peak cannot be used without it, in either direction, so buy it before you try to cross. It is not used in four areas: the Hive, Kingdom's Edge, Fog Canyon and Fungal Wastes.

sections.name: Vessel Fragments
sections.card:
Summary: Items that make your SOUL meter bigger. Every three fragments you gather combine into a Soul Vessel that adds 33 to your maximum. There are nine in the game, so three vessels in all, which doubles the SOUL you can hold.
Uses: SOUL kept in the vessels flows into the main meter on its own, after a short pause, whenever the main meter has space. Hitting enemies with the nail puts only 6 SOUL per hit into the vessels; any other way of getting SOUL fills them at the usual rate.
Tips: Sly in Dirtmouth sells two, for 550 Geo and 900 Geo; you must have found Sly in the Forgotten Crossroads first, and the second also needs the Shopkeeper's Key. The Seer gives one for 700 Essence, and the Ancient Basin fountain gives one when you drop 3000 Geo into it. Others lie in the world: one in Greenpath near the Queen's Gardens entrance that you cannot enter, one beside the lift in the Forgotten Crossroads once the City of Tears lift is unlocked, one near a lift above King's Station, and one in Deepnest over the tram that works.

sections.name: Quick Focus
sections.card:
Summary: A charm that makes you focus SOUL about a third faster. Salubra sells it for 800 Geo, in the Forgotten Crossroads.
Uses: Healing mid-fight becomes much more forgiving. It can let you heal in spots where you would otherwise get interrupted, or heal twice where you could normally manage only one. The short start-up before a focus begins is not made any faster.
Tips: It is most useful in fights with a lot of combat, such as bosses and arena fights like the Colosseum of Fools. With Deep Focus, which slows focusing, it cancels part of that slowdown, though the two together cost 7 notches. With Stalwart Shell, the invincibility lasts just long enough for you to focus and heal, and pairing it with Soul Catcher or Soul Eater makes healing more frequent and safer.

sections.name: Wayward Compass
sections.card:
Summary: A charm that shows where you are on the map. Iselda in Dirtmouth sells it for 220 Geo once you have met Cornifer.
Uses: The map marks where you are standing, including in areas whose map you have not bought yet.
Tips: It suits exploring, especially on a first playthrough. Before a boss fight, put on a charm built for combat instead.

sections.name: Tram Pass
sections.card:
Summary: An item found in a wrecked tram, in Deepnest's Failed Tramway. It lets you ride the trams.
Uses: Each tram needs the pass only once, put into the tram's door or into a mechanism at any of its stations. If you use a station mechanism while no tram is there, even for a tram you have not yet activated, it both switches the tram on and calls it to you.
Tips: Five places take the pass. North of Gruz Mother's arena, in the south-east Forgotten Crossroads, it starts the tram to the Resting Grounds. In the north-west Resting Grounds it starts the tram back to the Crossroads. East of the Hot Spring, in south-east Deepnest, it starts the tram to the Ancient Basin. North of Cornifer, in the north-east Ancient Basin, it starts the tram to both Deepnest and Kingdom's Edge. And west of the Hive, in the south-west of Kingdom's Edge, it starts the tram to the Ancient Basin.
